$ cat testdata/checks/paths.txt
export evaluate: parse has no cell of export/prices
export evaluate: resolve has no cell of export/prices
export evaluate: through resolve, parse, import
export import: through no lift
$ go test  # used-fewer-a
    the lifts parse and resolve are used by ./b on the path testdata/export/ → import → parse and past it, and ., which owns them, doesn't run them over testdata/export/, so no package writes their cells of that corpus's cases, which ./b's cells past them are built through.
        A package that uses a lift reaches it from each corpus by the path the lift's owner does. In ., register the corpus type of testdata/export/, and give import to hypercase.Use, so . runs them over testdata/export/ too. If . registers them already, or ./b doesn't reach them from testdata/export/, a registry is stale: run FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./..., which rewrites the registry of every package with tests.
--- FAIL: TestCorpus
    --- PASS: TestCorpus/script
    --- PASS: TestCorpus/checks
        --- PASS: TestCorpus/checks/paths
FAIL
[exit 1]

    the lifts parse and resolve are used by ./b on the path testdata/export/ → import → parse and past it, and ., which owns them, doesn't run them over testdata/export/, so no package writes their cells of that corpus's cases, which ./b's cells past them are built through.
        A package that uses a lift reaches it from each corpus by the path the lift's owner does, and the registry of . records the corpus type of testdata/export/ and the lifts on ./b's path from it, so a registry is stale: run FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./..., which rewrites the registry of every package with tests.
    testdata/export/prices.txtar: no registry claims out/parse/outcome: no column named parse runs over the corpus export.
        If a column should write them, register the column. If not, delete them by hand; FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./... leaves them in place.
    testdata/export/prices.txtar: no registry claims out/resolve/outcome: no column named resolve runs over the corpus export.
        If a column should write them, register the column. If not, delete them by hand; FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./... leaves them in place.
